pr_title: Fix up nullability and primitive type handing in schema generation
pr_body:
- Use `IsGetNullable` and `IsSetNullable` properties to set nullability status for properties
- Use per-instance `NullabilityInfoContext` instead of shared static instance
- Avoid allocating schemas for select primitive types
- Avoid including special `?` character in reference ID for nullable schemas
- Massage representation of `object` schemas to close https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/56351

Addresses feedback from https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/56330#discussion_r1649371307 and https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/56318

issue_context.title: object property causes build crash when generating OpenAPI document at build time
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

In a project using the Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server package to generate the OpenAPI document at build time, the build crashes if a class that will have a generated schema contains a property declared as type "object".

### Expected Behavior

a) the build should not crash
b) the schema for the property should have no `type` assertion -- the property's value can be any type.

### Steps To Reproduce

Declare a property in a class used as a response body like:
```
public object Object { get; set; }
```

review_comments: Is `Null` ok in the name here?

This calls into the overload that never exempts primitives so we're covered here. `JsonTypeInfoExtensionsTests.GetSchemaReferenceId_Works` has test cases to cover generics/enumerables with primitive types so we cover this case.

The JsonInfo for `object` types marks them as nullable but we want to maintain an empty "catch-all" schema for them in OpenAPI (no type, no format, no constraints) so we exempt them from this check here. I'll add a comment about this above.

It looks like that API is limited to properties that are sourced from a constructor parameter? This particular case applies to parameters source from the handler method, such as `name` in`app.MapGet("/", (string name) => ...)`. I don't think there's a JSON info-based API for that?
Ah yes, you're correct. You're on your own when it comes to method parameters.

One thing you might want to be aware of is that `NullabilityInfoContext` has a feature switch that can turn it off (resulting in exceptions being thrown every time you call its APIs). We learned this the hard way because the blazor sdk was turning it off by default, so I had to introduce defensive code in the STJ side that [checked for the feature switch](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/102852) before exercising `NullabilityInfoContext` APIs.

We decided in API review that the feature switch was a bad idea and we're going to remove it [at some point](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/103298#issuecomment-2161338112), though I'm not sure we'll be able to get to that for .NET 9.

I just deleted the feature switch altogether from runtime, so assuming you only target .NET 9 you should be good.
